proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7 caps liability but contains no Contractor indemnity, so we have added our standard one covering IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct. We can discuss the usual exclusions (our modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies as a fallback.

ops.text: (d) Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) Contractor's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Company data or Confidential Information caused by Contractor; or (iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Company shall give prompt notice of the claim, and Contractor shall have control of the defence and settlement with Company's reasonable cooperation, provided that no settlement imposing any obligation on Company shall be made without Company's consent.

proposal.summary: Insert Contractor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and misconduct

quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.
rationale: Despite the heading, Section 7 contains no indemnity language at all in either direction, and Section 5(c)'s non-infringement warranty is a bare representation with no defence or indemnity obligation and no remedy. There is no Contractor IP indemnity anywhere in the document, so we have inserted our standard Contractor indemnity (IP, breach of law, data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with a standard procedure.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

quote: all drawings, documents, designs, models, inventions, computer programs, computer systems, data, computer documentation and other tangible materials authored or prepared by Contractor for Company as the work product required by a Statement of Work (collectively, the "Works"), are the property of Company
rationale: The Works vest in Company, Contractor keeps only its pre-existing tools and know-how, and Section 4(c) grants a perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to any Contractor Information embedded in the Works; Section 4(d) confirms our right to modify and engage others. Nothing assigns our IP or data to Contractor and there is no joint ownership. We note ownership is conditioned on payment of the relevant invoice and there is no express Customer Data ownership sentence — points to raise, not deviations.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
sectionRef: § 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need the cap set at the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim, and our playbook requires confidentiality, data/security, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement to sit outside the cap for both parties. We have kept your existing structure and mutuality.

ops.newText: EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO EXCLUDED CLAIMS AND CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID OR PAYABLE TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM.
ops.oldText: EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES.

ops.text: "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS; COMPANY'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE SHALL NOT BE SUBJECT TO THE LIMITATIONS IN THIS PARAGRAPH 7(a).

proposal.summary: Make the cap 12 months' fees and add uncapped Excluded Claims

quote: CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES.
rationale: The cap is mutual and indirect damages are mutually excluded, but the only carve-out is Paragraph 9 (independent-contractor/tax obligations) — there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement, which the fallback requires. The basis is also fees paid for the specific SOW Services rather than 12 months' fees, which can fall well below six months' fees on a short task-based engagement. Redline sets the 12-month basis, adds an Excluded Claims sentence and confirms our payment obligations sit outside the cap.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a consent requirement that captures internal reorganisations or an M&A transaction, so we have added the customary affiliate/successor carve-out on written notice; the consent standard for other assignments is unchanged.

ops.newText: without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld; provided that either party may assign this Agreement in its entirety, upon written notice and without the other party's consent, to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, and no change of control of Company shall give Contractor any right to terminate or re-price this Agreement.
ops.oldText: without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out on notice

quote: Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
rationale: The consent requirement is mutual and reasonableness-qualified, but there is no carve-out allowing us to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger or asset sale, which the fallback requires; on its face our internal reorganisations and M&A transactions need Contractor's consent. Redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out on written notice and confirms a change of control gives Contractor no termination or re-pricing right.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

quote: Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services")
rationale: The engagement is expressly task-by-task via Statements of Work with no "sole and exclusive provider" or requirements-purchasing language in Sections 1 or 3, so we retain full freedom to use other suppliers.

quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination.
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalties, early-termination fee or minimum charge is payable by Company — termination only triggers payment for Services actually performed, and Section 5(d) even relieves us of fees where Contractor breaches the anti-bribery covenant. Nothing to redline.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our licences must cover our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and must be irrevocable and transferable to a successor; we have made those minimal changes to the existing grant without touching Contractor's ownership of its background IP.

ops.newText: Contractor hereby grants to Company, its affiliates and its contractors acting on Company's behalf a royalty-free, non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual and irrevocable license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations, which license is transferable to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Company's assets.
ops.oldText: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.

proposal.summary: Extend Contractor Information licence to affiliates/contractors, make it irrevocable and transferable

quote: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: The grant runs to Company alone: affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are excluded with no mechanism to add them, the licence is not stated to be irrevocable, and it is not transferable to a successor (Section 10 restricts assignment). That fails the fallback (affiliates on notice; transferable in an M&A transaction). Redline makes minimal additions to the existing grant without disturbing Contractor's ownership of its background IP.
sectionRef: § 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.

quote: Company acknowledges that Contractor provides consulting and development services to other clients, and agrees that nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed or construed to prevent Contractor from delivering on such business.
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds Company; the only "competition" language preserves Contractor's freedom to serve other clients, which does not restrict us. We note Section 4(b)(ii) restricts our resale/use of Contractor's own materials, but that is a licence-scope point (addressed under LICENSE), not a restrictive covenant.
sectionRef: § 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] As drafted we can only exit when no Statement of Work is outstanding, which is no convenience right at all in practice; we need to terminate the Agreement or any SOW on 30 days' notice with a refund of prepaid amounts, while Contractor's convenience right moves to 90 days' notice.

ops.newText: (a) Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any or no reason upon thirty (30) days advance notice to Contractor, in which case Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees for Services not performed as of the effective date of termination and no early termination charge or penalty shall apply. At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, Contractor may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon ninety (90) days advance notice to Company.
ops.oldText: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.

proposal.summary: Give Company convenience termination of any SOW on 30 days' notice; extend Contractor's notice to 90 days

quote: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
rationale: The term is evergreen (Section 2) but the convenience right is available only when no Statement of Work is outstanding, so we have no ability to exit an in-flight engagement — effectively no Customer convenience right, which fails the fallback. Contractor's 15-day convenience notice is also far short of the 90 days we require. Redline gives Company 30 days' convenience termination of the Agreement or any SOW with a prepaid-fee refund and moves Contractor to 90 days.

quote: Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced
rationale: There is no audit, inspection or verification right running against Company anywhere in the document; the records obligations run in our favour (Contractor must supply invoice detail and receipts), and Section 1(c) gives Contractor no access rights beyond compliance with our own security policies.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Arizona is outside our accepted list; we have moved governing law and venue to New York (Delaware, California or England and Wales are acceptable alternatives) and seated any arbitration in New York County.

ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof, and the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement.
ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.

ops.newText: will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration seated in New York County, New York pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com).
ops.oldText: will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com).

proposal.summary: New York law and New York County courts; arbitration, if retained, seated in New York

quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
rationale: Arizona law is outside our accepted list (New York preferred; Delaware, California or England and Wales as fallback), so this fails the fallback. Disputes are also pushed into mandatory USA&M arbitration with no stated seat, whereas we require courts. Redline moves governing law and exclusive venue to New York County and, if arbitration is retained, seats it there.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

quote: During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
rationale: Section 3 contains no most-favoured-nation mechanic in either direction, so there is no obligation on us to extend Contractor best terms or match third-party offers. Nothing to redline.

quote: Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
rationale: Compensation is time-and-materials under each Statement of Work on a task-by-task basis, with no minimum hours, retainer, take-or-pay commitment, shortfall charge or volume cap binding Company.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services
rationale: This sits at our fallback: mutual, limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services, 12 months post-termination, and a solicitation (not no-hire) restriction. We note it lacks express carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches — a drafting point we would raise but not a deviation.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

quote: The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.
rationale: There is no automatic renewal, no renewal term and no non-renewal notice window, so none of the walk-away risks arise; the evergreen term is more favourable to us than a renewing term. We note Section 3(b) lets Contractor change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap — a price-predictability point we would raise (lesser of CPI and 3%) rather than a renewal deviation.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement is silent on exit, so we have added transition assistance for up to six months at your then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any reason, Contractor shall (i) at Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Contractor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days, return to Company all Company data, Confidential Information and Works (including works in progress) in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete Company data and Confidential Information from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and deletion certification on exit

quote: Upon receipt of final payment Contractor shall provide to Company, and will assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.
rationale: Termination only addresses final payment and assignment of works in progress; there is no transition assistance, no obligation to return our data or Confidential Information in a usable format, no timeline and no deletion certification (Section 8 imposes no return obligation either). Redline inserts the standard exit paragraph: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, data return within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 5 contains no conformance warranty or remedy, so we have added our fallback: professional and workmanlike Services plus 90 days' conformity to Specifications, remedied by re-performance, repair, replacement or refund.

ops.text: (c)(i) Contractor represents and warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards and that, for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Work will conform in all material respects to the applicable Specifications and documentation. Company's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Contractor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Work. Contractor further warrants that the Works will not contain any virus, malicious or disabling code.

proposal.summary: Insert a 90-day conformance warranty with a repair/re-perform/refund remedy

quote: THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE IN LIEU OF ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
rationale: Section 5 gives only legal-compliance (knowledge-qualified), authority and non-infringement representations — there is no warranty that the Works conform to the Specifications, no warranty period and no remedy, and the implied warranties are disclaimed, so there is no usable conformance warranty at any level. The professional and workmanlike standard in Section 1(b) is a performance covenant without a remedy. Redline inserts the fallback 90-day conformance warranty with re-performance/repair/replacement/refund and a no-malicious-code warranty.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Contractor accesses our records and systems, so we need cyber/privacy cover alongside the existing CGL and E&O lines; we have set it at the USD 2M fallback level.

ops.text: In addition, where Contractor processes, stores or has access to Company data, Confidential Information or Company systems, Contractor shall maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000).

proposal.summary: Add cyber liability cover for a vendor accessing Company data and systems

quote: Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)
rationale: Workers' comp, CGL USD 1M and E&O USD 1M are in place with certificates on request, but there is no cyber/privacy cover even though Contractor obtains our records, data and access to our computer systems (Sections 1(c) and 8) — the fallback requires E&O USD 1M plus cyber USD 2M. Redline adds a single cyber line at the fallback level; the lower E&O and missing CGL aggregate limits are points we would raise but not press.
